- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true peak by 1–3 days.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window; true prices often revert to lower levels after a peak, while model holds high values.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true prices show downward momentum or volatility.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — it doesn’t adjust quickly to sudden drops or spikes in the true price series.
- When true prices are below 70, model often remains above 70, suggesting a persistent upward bias in low-price regimes.
- Model’s forecast slope is too steep — it assumes a linear or accelerating trend, while true prices often show volatility and non-linear corrections.
- Model tends to ignore recent low-price corrections and overweights earlier high-price data, leading to overconfidence in upward bias.
